Logging._LogLevel: What reaches the log, per category. Flower is set to Debug so this server's own deliberate Debug lines - a request dropped for being outside the allowed networks, a play event ignored as already applied - actually appear, without turning ASP.NET Core's per-request Information noise back on. Raising Flower:LogLevel below to Verbose additionally enables the per-tick Trace lines; both have to allow a line for it to be written.

Flower._LogLevel: Serilog's floor for every sink. Debug by default. Verbose turns on the per-tick diagnostic lines - discovery polls, signature-check detail - which are silent otherwise.
Flower._DataDirectory: Where flower.db, the device key, the peer files and the logs live. Empty means the per-OS user data location (~/Library/Application Support/Flower/Server, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Flower\Server, ~/.local/share/Flower/Server). Set it for a container or a dedicated data volume. Everything else below can also be set in flower-server.json inside that directory, which is the better place for it - this file is part of the deployment, that one is part of the data.
Flower._AdvertisedHost: Optional. Host:port to put in pairing QR codes when the address a device should dial isn't the one the request arrived on (reverse proxy, remapped container port).
Flower._Alias: Optional. The name this server shows up as in a Flower client's sidebar. Defaults to the machine name.
Flower._AdvertiseOnLan: Announce this server over mDNS so clients find it without being given an address. Turn off for tailnet/reverse-proxy-only deployments.
Flower._WebUiPath: Optional override for where the browser UI lives. Normally empty: the bundle is built next to this binary by Flower.Server's own build, and the data directory is checked after that. Set it, and it becomes the only place looked at. A server without a bundle still serves its API; only the browser settings page is unavailable.
